title: The engineers that build rivers
text: Beavers {{1}} vanished from Britain by the sixteenth century, hunted {{2}} their fur, their scent glands and their supposed medicinal powers. {{3}} was not until 2009 that a licensed trial released a family of beavers on a Devon river, {{4}} the animals immediately began doing what beavers do: felling willows, damming streams and digging channels. {{5}} is their impact on water flow {{6}} scientists now describe beaver wetlands as a natural flood-defence, holding water on the land {{7}} a sponge and releasing it slowly. Water companies and insurers have taken notice, since beaver engineering can be dramatically cheaper {{8}} concrete — and the concrete, unlike the beavers, never reproduces.
